title: Cloud session to main: how the work gets back to your PC

system_description.seeded:
Assembled from the declared sources; you may open the cited URLs. The repository is an example that you cannot open, so its facts are quoted in full here: check against these quotes.
  - Claude Code docs, scheduled-tasks comparison table: "Access to local files | No (fresh clone)" for cloud sessions.
  - https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web.md: "repository cloning and pull request creation require GitHub." / "When a session completes, you can create a PR from claude.ai/code." / start from the CLI with `claude --cloud "Fix the authentication bug in src/auth/login.ts"`.
  - The repo's git remote is GitHub (git@github.com:example-org/garden-journal.git); its default branch is main, and the current branch is main.
  - https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pull: `git pull --rebase` fetches, then rebases the current branch on top of the upstream branch, so your local commits are replayed after the remote's; `git push` then sends them. A conflict stops the merge or rebase and leaves it for you to resolve.
  - git config pull.rebase=false, so a plain `git pull` fetches and merges the remote branch into the current local branch.
